target.title: fix(diagnostics-otel): set CLIENT span kind on model call and tool execution spans
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

All OpenClaw trace spans use `SpanKind.INTERNAL` by default, making external API calls (LLM providers, tool executions) invisible as distinct dependency nodes in distributed tracing tools. Model call spans (model.call.*) only got `CLIENT` kind when the `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental` opt-in was set; tool execution spans (tool.execution.*) never carried an explicit kind at all.

- Problem: Trace visualization tools (Jaeger, Zipkin) show all spans as flat internal operations — no way to distinguish network latency from processing time
- Solution: Set `SpanKind.CLIENT` unconditionally on model call spans and on actual tool execution spans (started/completed/error). Blocked tool spans (policy-denied, no outgoing request) keep the implicit `INTERNAL` default.
- What changed: `extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.ts` (modelCallSpanKind + 3 actual tool span sites; blocked path unchanged), `service.test.ts` (updated assertions + blocked span test), `docs/gateway/opentelemetry.md` (docs reflect kind is no longer gated)
- What did NOT change: GenAI semconv span naming/attributes remain gated behind `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN`; model.failover, context.assembled, and other internal-only spans keep their existing kind behavior

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all)

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [ ] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Fixes #102017
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

The OpenTelemetry SpanKind specification defines `CLIENT` for outgoing requests to external services. LLM API calls (OpenAI, xAI, Ollama, etc.) and tool executions (shell commands, HTTP requests, filesystem operations) semantically represent client requests. Using `INTERNAL` for these spans breaks distributed tracing — latency analysis cannot distinguish network round-trips from internal processing, and dependency graphs in Jaeger/Zipkin cannot show external service dependencies.

## Evidence

- Behavior addressed: Model call and tool execution spans now carry `SpanKind.CLIENT` (value 2) instead of the default `SpanKind.INTERNAL`
- Real environment tested: Linux Node 24, branch `fix/otel-span-kind-client-102017`
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:

```bash
# Run the full test suite
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts
```

- Evidence after fix:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts

 RUN  v4.1.9

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  108 passed (108)

# Source-level verification:

# modelCallSpanKind() now unconditionally returns CLIENT:
$ grep -A 3 "function modelCallSpanKind" extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.ts
function modelCallSpanKind(): SpanKind {
  return SpanKind.CLIENT;
}

# 3 actual tool.execution span creation points carry kind=CLIENT:
$ grep -B 1 "kind: SpanKind.CLIENT" extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.ts
            kind: SpanKind.CLIENT,    # tool.execution.started
            kind: SpanKind.CLIENT,    # tool.execution.completed
            kind: SpanKind.CLIENT,    # tool.execution.error

# Blocked tool span has no explicit kind (INTERNAL default):
$ grep -A 5 "outcome.*blocked" extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.ts | grep -c "kind"
0

# Assertions verifying the span kind values:
$ grep -B 1 "kind).toBe" extensions/diagnostics-otel/src/service.test.ts
expect(modelOptions?.kind).toBe(2);                  # model call span
expect(toolOptions?.kind).toBe(2);                   # tool execution span
expect(Object.hasOwn(blockedOptions ?? {}, "kind")).toBe(false);  # blocked span
```

- Observed result after fix:
  1. Model call spans (model.call.submitted/completed/error) always export with `SpanKind.CLIENT` — no longer gated behind `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN`
  2. Actual tool execution spans (tool.execution.started/completed/error) always export with `SpanKind.CLIENT`
  3. Blocked tool spans (policy-denied, no outgoing request) keep `SpanKind.INTERNAL` — semantically correct
  4. GenAI semconv env var continues to control span naming (openclaw.model.call vs gen_ai.*) independently
  5. Internal-only spans (model.failover, context.assembled, memory.pressure, session.stuck) remain `SpanKind.INTERNAL`
- What was not tested: Live Jaeger/Zipkin collector ingestion (requires external infrastructure). Unit test assertions verify the correct kind value is set on span options.

## Root Cause (if applicable)

PR #86191 (`f824e1596ad`) introduced `modelCallSpanKind()` which only returned `SpanKind.CLIENT` when `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN=gen_ai_latest_experimental` was set, otherwise `undefined` → `INTERNAL`. Tool execution spans were added without any kind override since their introduction.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

The test suite (`service.test.ts`) has four assertions specific to span kind:
- Default model call: `expect(modelOptions?.kind).toBe(2)` (was `toBe(false)` for absent kind)
- Tool execution (error path): `expect(toolOptions?.kind).toBe(2)` (new)
- Tool execution (content capture): `expect(toolOptions?.kind).toBe(2)` (new)
- Blocked tool span: `expect(Object.hasOwn(blockedOptions ?? {}, "kind")).toBe(false)` (new, focused test)

108 tests pass.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

None directly visible to end users. Trace data consumers (Jaeger, Zipkin, Grafana Tempo, Datadog) will see `kind=CLIENT` on model call and tool execution spans, enabling proper dependency graphs and latency breakdown.

## Security Impact (required)

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified scenarios: Source-level verification of all relevant span creation points; test assertion updates checked for correctness
- Edge cases checked: GenAI semconv opt-in still controls span names/attributes independently; tool spans that go through the trusted span tracking path (takeTrackedTrustedSpan) inherit the same kind from the original span
- What you did NOT verify: Live Jaeger collector round-trip; non-Node runtimes

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — span kind change only affects how trace backends classify spans, not runtime behavior
- [x] Config/env changes? Only the documentation of `OTEL_SEMCONV_STABILITY_OPT_IN` — no actual config surface changed
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes. Unconditional CLIENT for model calls + CLIENT for actual tool executions, blocked tool spans kept INTERNAL. No new config or env var needed.
- **Refactor needed**: No. The changes are self-contained in 5 locations within one file.
- **Alternative considered**: Keeping the GenAI-semconv gate but changing span kind to always be CLIENT regardless of naming — this is what we implemented. Another option was adding a new config knob for span kind per span type, which would be over-engineered for this use case.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **Co-Authored-By**: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest risk area**: None significant. SpanKind is a classification tag on exported spans — changing from INTERNAL to CLIENT affects trace visualization only, not runtime behavior, data paths, or permission checks.
- **Mitigation**: All existing span names, attributes, and lifecycle are preserved. The change is opt-in only at the trace-consumer level (users who export traces to Jaeger/Zipkin will see the improvement).
- **Compatibility**: Users currently ingesting OpenClaw traces who have built dashboards/filters based on `kind=INTERNAL` will need to update those filters. No users have reported relying on the INTERNAL kind value.

Fixes #102017
